To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

i) the SOS response is involved in stress-inducibility of biofilm formation; ii) LexA contributes to both normal and stress-induced biofilm formation; and iii) DNA degradation in the biofilm matrix renders the biofilm susceptible to stress.

SOS involvement in stress-induced biofilm formation is dependent on RecA, that the wild-type lexA is required for both normal and stress-induced biofilm formation, that the DNA replication inhibitor, hydroxyurea, stimulates biofilm formation, and that the biofilm matrix is a source of stress for the bacteria.
